newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai commodity exchange to move to Pudong.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai commodity exchange to move to Pudong.

text.p: The Shanghai Commodity Exchange has bought land in the Pudong development zone for a new exchange building, the Shanghai Securities Newspaper said on Thursday.
Construction of the new exchange, with a total floor area of 15,000 square metres, will start in 1997, the newspaper said.
Shanghai Commodity Exchange is the biggest of Shanghai's three futures exchanges in terms of trading volume, which reached 1.94 trillion yuan in 1995.
The city government has ordered all Shanghai's major financial markets to move to Pudong, which it hopes will eventually become the Wall Street of Asia.
The Shanghai Cereals & Oils Exchange will move to Pudong by the end of 1996, the Shanghai Stock Exchange in July 1997 and the Shanghai Metal Exchange at the beginning of 1998.
